bangul--yellow-mountain.scene: INTRODUCING BANGUL, fifteen, Kim Yushin's nephew — young, brave, and in a hurry. The Silla lines on the Yellow Mountain plain, a hot summer afternoon, after the fourth failed charge. Low three-quarter angle from beside his father's stirrup: Bangul has just come at a run and stands at the stirrup, chest still heaving, looking UP at his mounted father (only an out-of-focus armoured knee, stirrup and horse flank at the frame edge), his body already half-turned to go, one fist wound tight in the reins of his own horse just out of frame. No weapon in frame. He answers quietly: "I have heard you, Father." A boy's smooth face gone very steady — brows level, lips pressed, eyes bright and wet but unafraid, the ghost of a brave small smile. The tails of his red crescent-moon headband stream in the hot wind. Behind him the yellow-dust plain rolls away under a vast summer storm sky: towering sunlit cloud, drifting battle dust in ochre and gold, a far Baekje stockade on a rise with tiny banners, all soft and out of focus. Hard afternoon sun breaking through cloud rakes across his face from the side; cool sky-blue (#5e9dd8) lives in the shadows and on the white silk.

gwanchang--yellow-mountain.scene: INTRODUCING GWANCHANG, sixteen, a hwarang so young they had to pad the helmet. The Silla command line on the Yellow Mountain plain, late afternoon, every general watching. High over-the-shoulder angle from horseback: his father's pointing gloved hand and grey-and-crimson sleeve, dark and out of focus, cut into the foreground corner, aimed at the boy like a finger on a map. Gwanchang stands below in front of the horse and looks UP into that hand, chin lifted, answering before anyone else can: "Yes." A smooth boy's face lit with eager, reckless courage — bright eyes with red liner wings, a quick fierce grin. He hugs a steel Silla helmet far too big for him under one arm, its rim stuffed with folded cloth padding; his other fist grips a long spear upright. Blue crescent-moon headband, white hwarang po with crimson collar and sash. Behind him dust blows across the yellow plain under a huge churning summer sky; horses and blue Silla banners are dark soft shapes in ochre haze. A low sun through the dust rakes across his face from the side, warm gold, with ice-blue (#79b6f2) in the shadows and on the helmet's steel.

pumil--yellow-mountain.scene: INTRODUCING KIM PUMIL, a Silla general with a son in the ranks — he knows exactly where the boy is standing. The Silla command line on the Yellow Mountain plain, the battle going badly. Low angle from the ground beside his horse: Pumil sits his saddle in his grey-white robes with crimson collar and cuffs, his bare hand held straight out, one finger pointing DOWN past the camera at his own son the way a man points at a map, and tells the generals, flat and level: "My son is only sixteen… can he be the mark the three armies aim by?" A tired, weathered face held perfectly still — heavy-lidded eyes, jaw locked, mouth a hard line — and only the eyes giving him away, wet and red-rimmed. His horse's dark neck and mane cut across the foreground. Behind him a heavy dust-storm sky over the yellow plain: churning ochre dust, grey-blue cloud, far Silla banners as soft shapes of PLAIN solid blue cloth with no emblems, symbols or characters on them. A shaft of late sun through the dust rakes across his face from the side, with steel-blue (#6a8ab8) in the shadows of the silk.

munmu-king--kim-chunchu.scene: INTRODUCING KING MUNMU — Bupmin, taking his dead father's crown. The Silla palace hall in Seorabeol at first light, the morning after King Chunchu dies; mourning incense still hangs in the air. Low three-quarter angle from below: Bupmin, in the king's crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery and blue shoulder pieces, raises the gold Silla crown in both hands and lowers it onto his own head, elbows high, the gold spangles and green jade pendants swinging. His usual cocky grin is gone: square jaw set hard under the goatee and moustache, eyes red-rimmed from the night and fixed straight ahead, lips pressed on one slow steadying breath — his father's charm with his uncle's spine. Behind him the hall dissolves into drifting blue-grey incense smoke: dim red pillars, white mourning banners hanging still, the soft warm bokeh of a hundred guttering candles. A cold dawn shaft through the open hall doors rakes across his face and the gold from the side, while crimson (#C41E3A) burns in the silk and in the candle haze.

wuzetian-empress--ungjin-commandery.scene: INTRODUCING WU ZETIAN, Empress of the Tang, in the season she begins to rule through her husband. Night in the Daming Palace in Chang'an. Low three-quarter angle across the imperial dais: she sits close beside the emperor's throne — he is only a blurred shape in imperial yellow at the frame edge — and leans in toward him, one hand resting lightly on the gilded arm of HIS throne as if it were already hers. Red lips curved in a slow, amused, dangerous smile, eyes half-lidded and sliding toward him: "Make it sound like an honour, Majesty." Her red silk court robe and gold hair ornaments exactly as on the sheet, Tang court dress, not hanbok. Behind her the hall melts into drifting incense haze: vermilion columns, a lattice door hard-backlit in gold, red lanterns blooming into warm bokeh, cool blue-green shadows pooling on the dark lacquered floor. A tall bronze oil lamp beside the throne rakes warm gold light across her face, her jewels and the silk, with rose-pink (#e879a6) in the highlights.

liurengui--ungjin-commandery.scene: INTRODUCING THE BLACK TORTOISE, Liu Rengui — a Tang general of sixty, disgraced last year, and in an excellent mood. He has come east to Baekje to hold what the Tang broke. A late-autumn afternoon on the riverbank below a burned Baekje fortress on a cliff: he has just stepped off a Tang boat. Low three-quarter angle: he strides up the bank and holds one hand out palm-up to an aide off-frame for the calendar scroll, with a dry, delighted, crinkle-eyed smile: "Heaven means to make an old man rich, it seems." His FACE is fully lit and clearly drawn (the sheet is only a dark silhouette): a lean, upright old man, long narrow face, deep-set patient eyes, a long grey moustache and long thin grey beard, grey hair under a black Tang futou cap. Tang mingguang armour with two round polished chest discs is strapped over a plain undyed WHITE commoner's robe instead of rank colours; a brush-and-tablet case hangs at his belt. Behind him: the broad river in pale gold mist, a Tang boat's mast and furled sail, the charred fortress walls on the cliff as soft shapes. A low autumn sun rakes across his face from the side, with slate-green (#3d4a48) in the cool shadows.

boksin--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING GWISHIL BOKSIN, the Baekje general who raised a dead country once — and kept the receipts. A frost-bitten mountain stockade in the Baekje hills at winter dusk, the season after the capital fell. Low three-quarter angle from beside a campfire: he sits hunched on an upturned supply crate, the long red-lacquered shaft leaning against his shoulder, and counts a bundle of notched bamboo tally sticks through his thick fingers one by one, scowling at the sum, lips moving. Bald crown with one long black topknot tail tied in red cord, heavy scowling brows, black moustache and pointed beard; black-lacquered lamellar with heavy rounded shoulder guards over his slate-blue robe. Blunt, managerial, faintly menacing. Behind him a timber palisade and blue snowy ridges dissolve into woodsmoke and falling snow; far back, tiny and blurred, a line of roped prisoners in Tang dress. The campfire lights him from below in hard bronze-gold (#a8781f), with embers drifting up past his face.

tenji--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING THE EASTERN PRINCE of Yamato — he does the arithmetic before anyone asks for it. Winter in the palace hall at Asuka, the day a Baekje envoy arrives with a hundred roped Tang prisoners as a present. Low three-quarter angle from the floor: he sits on the raised hall floor in his wide slate-navy court robe brocaded with faded gold peony scrolls, tapping his flat wooden shaku tablet against his palm, head turned and eyes cutting hard SIDEWAYS toward the envoy off-frame at the left edge, a thin, dry, unimpressed half-smile: "A hundred prisoners. Generous… When do they show us the rest of the bill?" High black topknot under a small black lacquered upright cap, thin moustache, pointed black goatee. Yamato court dress, never an Edo kimono. The hall around him is dim and smoky: dark vermilion pillars sinking into deep umber shadow, brazier smoke curling; far behind, one narrow open door is a slot of cold blue snowy courtyard in soft bokeh. A bronze brazier of glowing coals on the floor beside him throws hard warm amber firelight up across his face and the gold brocade, with rose-pink (#e06a95) in the sheen of the silk.

abe--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING ABE NO HIRAFU, Yamato's admiral of the cold north — he has fought on ice, and never on this river. The same winter palace hall at Asuka. Dutch-tilted low angle: the huge bearded seafarer lurches up off his knees, one fist thumping his chest and the other flung out toward the west, laughing into the hall: "Send me! I've crossed the cold sea… I'll bring you back their emperor's hat!" Wild black hair in a rough topknot, full black beard, heavy brows, eyes crinkled with laughter, mouth wide open. Grey wolf-fur mantle over a long red cape, a blue-grey quilted coat printed with pale leaves, red cord sash. No weapon in frame. Behind him vermilion pillars and white plaster walls melt into brazier smoke and cold daylight from the open doors, snow drifting outside as soft bokeh. A brazier just below the frame throws hard red-orange (#c8463c) light up across his beard, the fur and his face.

saimei--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING THE EASTERN EMPRESS of Yamato, sixty-six — she has outlived two reigns and most of her ministers' opinions. The same winter palace hall at Asuka; she has let everyone talk, and now she speaks once. Low angle from the floor below her dais: she sits perfectly upright and immovable, her white silk train spread around her, and lifts one hand barely an inch — the whole hall stops — eyes half-lidded, mouth calm: "Bring him the sword. The one with seven branches." Ageless powdered face, red lips, a small vermilion mark on the brow, long grey hair loose past the shoulders, a white silk head-wrap with hanging braided cords under a small gold openwork crown; layered white robes with wide celadon-green borders patterned in pale-gold cloud scrolls, a long vermilion tasselled cord. Yamato court dress, never a kimono or hanbok. The hall around her is dim and smoky: dark vermilion pillars sinking into deep umber shadow, incense curling through the air, one far open door a narrow slot of cold blue snowy light. A tall standing oil lamp right beside the dais throws hard warm gold light across her face and the white silk from the side, carving deep painted shadows into every fold, with soft pink (#f090b0) glinting in the silk's sheen.

takutsu--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING ECHI NO TAKUTSU, a Yamato captain — loud, loyal, and fond of a country that isn't his. The shingle beach below the cliff fortress of Juryu, a windy autumn afternoon. Low three-quarter angle from the stones: he has just bowed long and low to the sea he crossed, and now straightens and turns back toward the Baekje generals, one fist pressed over his heart, about to say the one thing he prepared: "No one in this country knows my name. So instead of mine, I will say yours." Young clean-shaven face, straight brows, steady dark eyes bright with plain earnest conviction, jaw set; the long tails of his WHITE headband snap sideways in the sea wind. Orange-red robe with ochre-gold collar, black-lacquered cuirass with square black shoulder flaps on gold cords. Framed tight, CHEST-UP, cut just above the sash: his hips and his sword stay below the frame edge, no sword or hilt visible. Behind him a grey-green sea churns under a huge torn autumn sky, white surf, the dark hulls and furled sails of Yamato boats soft and out of focus, gulls wheeling. A low gold sun breaking through cloud over the sea rakes across his face from the side, with dusty rose (#b05575) in the shadows and the silk.

dochim--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING DOCHIM, a monk with a general's staff, in no hurry about either. The shingle beach below the cliff fortress of Juryu, the autumn roll call; everyone else stands to attention, and he introduces himself sitting down. Low three-quarter angle from beside him: he sits at ease on a flat rock above the tideline, the gilt staff with its ringed finial laid across his knees, a long string of black 108 beads running slowly through the fingers of one hand, and tilts his shaven head up toward the new king off-frame with a serene, patient, faintly amused smile, the way a monk smiles at a donor whose gift has not yet arrived: "The Buddha taught that all things are impermanent." Calm narrow eyes, small dark goatee. Ochre-gold robe under a red-orange kasaya fastened at the left shoulder with an iron ring. Behind him grey-green sea and white surf under a big autumn sky of drifting cloud, gulls, a low open wooden rowing boat beached on the shingle, and far up on the headland a soft KOREAN mountain fortress: long low grey stone ramparts along the cliff top with one curved black-tiled giwa gate pavilion — no towers, no keeps, no European castle. A low gold sun through the cloud rakes across his scalp, his face and the kasaya folds from the side, with warm amber (#a06a28) in the shadows.

sangji--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING HEUKCHI SANGJI, the biggest man on the beach, and the hardest to line up. The shingle beach below the cliff fortress of Juryu, the autumn roll call. Extreme worm's-eye angle from the stones at his feet: he has just stepped forward exactly one pace and stopped, towering against the sky like a wall, one gauntleted fist wrapped around the upright shaft of his long gilt-headed spear, and glowers straight down past the camera, deadpan and immovable: "Heukchi Sangji. Imjon. …That's it." Heavy brows drawn down, hard unblinking eyes, black moustache and short square beard, mouth a flat line. Black helm with a tall red plume whipping in the wind; black-lacquered lamellar with square shoulder guards over a maroon-red robe, tan cross-strap and wide tan belt. The spear is his only weapon in frame: no sword. Behind and above him a vast autumn sky of torn grey and gold cloud, gulls, and high on the dark cliff a soft KOREAN mountain fortress: long low grey stone ramparts stepping along the cliff top and one curved black-tiled giwa gate pavilion with upturned eaves — no towers, no keeps, no European castle. A low gold sun from the side rakes across his face and the lacquered plates, with deep ochre (#8a6b1f) in the shadows.

sateksangya--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING SATEK SANGYA, a Satek lord with harbour money and a general's patience. The shingle beach below the cliff fortress of Juryu, the autumn roll call; he has worn the tall gilt crown of his house for the occasion, and that is his only concession to it. Low three-quarter angle from beside a stack of straw rice bales: he sits on the bales with the harbour ledger half-unrolled across his knee, its page turned toward him and away from the camera so only the blank back of the paper shows, head bowed over it, NOT looking up, eyes narrowed at a sum, mouth flat and unimpressed: "Forty boats, eleven hundred bales of rice, thirty thousand arrows… Nobody has paid me yet." Sea-tanned stocky face, clipped black beard and moustache, thick neck. Deep red wide-sleeved robe with a black crossed collar under a plain grey steel lamellar vest; square-holed bronze coins on a cord at his dark sash. Behind him, soft and out of focus: beached cargo boats, coils of rope, grey-green surf under a broad autumn sky of drifting cloud. A low gold sun from the side rakes across his face, the gilt crown and the paper, with burnished gold (#b8933f) in the highlights.

pung-king--king-pungjang.scene: INTRODUCING KING PUNGJANG — crowned on a beach within an hour of landing. The shingle beach below the cliff fortress of Juryu, the autumn roll call: every general has announced himself, everyone now looks at the king, and nobody has given him a line. Low three-quarter angle from the stones: he stands in the king's red robe with dark-navy-lined sleeves and gold-scroll shoulders, one hand still settling the tall black silk Baekje royal cap with its twin openwork gold flame ornaments onto his head as if it might slip, and ad-libs with an uncertain, hopeful half-smile, brows lifted, eyes flicking sideways for approval: "I am Buyeo Pung, son of King Euija, and… king of— of Baekje. …Is that right?" Sharp face, small chin goatee, loose strands falling from the topknot. Behind him grey-green sea and white surf under a big autumn sky, soft and out of focus: the 7th-century Yamato boats that brought him — low open wooden hulls with a single mast, one plain square mat sail and rows of oars, never tall multi-masted European ships — and on the cliff a Korean stone rampart with one curved black-tiled giwa gate pavilion, no towers. A low gold sun breaking through cloud rakes across his face, the gold flames and the red silk from the side, with pale gold (#e6c76a) in the highlights.

namgun--pyongyang-i.scene: INTRODUCING YEON NAMGUN, Gesomun's second son — loud, loyal, and he believes everything he's told twice. On top of the grey stone wall of Pyongyang on a cold late-autumn afternoon, the Tang camps somewhere below. Low three-quarter angle along the parapet: he leans one elbow on a battlement and jabs a finger down at the stones under his feet, lecturing a young sentry who did not ask (only a blurred helmeted shoulder at the frame edge), chest out, chin up, booming with total conviction: "Pyongyang does not fall. Not since the Holy King strung his bow. Seven hundred years." Long black hair with a topknot bound in red cord, black moustache and beard, heavy earnest brows, eyes bright with certainty, a proud open grin. Grey lamellar laced in red over a red robe, red sash, a bow and quiver on his back. Behind him, soft and out of focus, the red two-tier gate pavilion with grey-tiled roofs on its stone ridge and towering grey-white clouds that look about to pick a side. A low sun breaking under the clouds rakes across his face from the side, with brick-red (#9e3b32) in the shadows and on the lacquer.

pangxiaotai--snake-river.scene: INTRODUCING THE WHITE TIGER, Pang Xiaotai — a Tang general who brought all his sons to war, to show them how it's done. The ford of the Snake River in deep winter: shallow grey water over gravel, snow on the banks, bare willows and dead reeds, mist on the far bank. Low angle from the water at his horse's knees: he rides into the ford on a big grey Tang warhorse, spray flying around its legs, and twists in the saddle to call back to his sons riding behind him (only blurred young riders and white pennants at the frame edge), one gloved arm sweeping forward across the river, laughing, sure the river is a road. His FACE is fully lit and clearly drawn (the sheet is only a dark ink silhouette): a broad, weathered southern face in his fifties, strong nose, deep laugh lines, a short grizzled black-and-grey beard, hair in a topknot tied with a long white cloth whose tails stream in the wind. Tang mingguang armour with round polished chest discs and lamellar shoulder guards over a white war robe. No sword in frame: one hand on the reins, one sweeping forward. A low winter sun breaking through cloud rakes across his face and the steel from the side, with silver-white (#c9c9c9) in the highlights and his breath steaming.

yung--white-river.scene: INTRODUCING PRINCE YUNG, Euija's eldest son — born to be crown prince; born is not the same as stays. The deck of the Tang flagship at the mouth of the White River, late summer, the fleet anchored across the river's throat, waiting for his younger brother's fleet. Low three-quarter angle from the deck: he stands at the wooden rail with both hands closed hard on it, face turned out toward the open water where his brother's banner will come, while an old Tang general at his shoulder (only a blurred white sleeve and armoured shoulder at the frame edge) asks whether he can look at it. He answers short and cold, then too quiet: "I have looked at worse. …I looked at my father." Same face as the sheet: high topknot, thin moustache, small chin beard; jaw locked, eyes dry and far away, mouth very still. NOT the red-and-gold Baekje robe from the sheet: he now wears a Tang officer's round-collared crimson robe with a black leather belt and a black futou cap tied at the back over the topknot. Behind him the wide grey-gold estuary, mudflats, reed beds and sandbars in haze, the batten sails of anchored Tang warships soft and out of focus. A low late-afternoon sun off the water rakes across his face from the side, muted gold (#d4b45a) in the light.

namseng-supreme--yeon-gesomun.scene: INTRODUCING YEON NAMSENG, Supreme Commander at thirty-one — his father's chair was built for one man, and it shows. The great hall at Pyongyang the morning after Yeon Gesomun's death: cold grey dawn through a tall window, last night's brazier burned down to embers, white mourning cloth hung over the red banners. Low three-quarter angle from the floor: he has just lowered himself into his father's huge carved wooden chair draped in a brown bear fur, and it swallows him: hands set too wide on the massive armrests, his back nowhere near the high backrest, empty fur all around him. He tries to sit the way his father sat, chin up, jaw set, but his eyes slide sideways toward the empty doorway, uncertain; a tired, heavy, swallowing look. Topknot, short beard and moustache, grey lamellar with a red scarf knotted at the throat, red sash. He has unbuckled his sword: NO sword, hilt or scabbard anywhere in frame, nothing over his shoulders but the fur. Behind him the dim hall in drifting smoke: red pillars, white mourning banners, cold blue window light and the last red glow of the embers. The cold dawn window light rakes across his face from the side while the embers glow warm below, with muted red (#c25a4e) in the shadows.

namsan--pyongyang-ii.scene: INTRODUCING YEON NAMSAN, Gesomun's youngest son — the one who listens at doors. On the grey stone wall of Pyongyang in the autumn of the last siege, the red two-tier gate pavilion behind him. Low three-quarter angle along the parapet: he crouches behind a battlement, one gauntleted hand flat on the cold stone, leaning close to his brother's ear (only a blurred armoured shoulder at the frame edge) and whispering, his eyes locked down over the wall on a rider in a Tang coat at the top of the gully below, out of frame: "Brother… he's wearing their coat." A stunned, quiet, sharp-eyed face: brows pinched, lips barely parted on the whisper, the look of a man who heard it first. Black round helm with a red plume and gold boss, short beard and moustache, grey lamellar edged in red, red cape knotted at the throat, red sash. No weapon in frame. Behind him smoke drifts up from the Tang camps across the valley, a field of soft enemy banners far below, heavy autumn clouds over the ridge. A low dusk sun through the smoke rakes across his face from the side, with dusty coral (#d4776a) in the light.

yushin-elder--pyongyang-ii.scene: INTRODUCING KIM YUSHIN at seventy-three — a rank above every rank; they had to invent it for him. The king's hall at Seorabeol in the tenth month, after Pyongyang has opened its gate; the young king has just cut a new grade above the seventeen and named it for him: Supreme General. Low three-quarter angle from the floor: the old marshal STANDS — he never sits — broad and heavy in a plain Silla-blue po with a plum-violet sash, taking the honour with one slow bow of the head, his big scarred hands folded before him, and a rare dry half-smile in the grey-streaked beard: "A new name for an old man." Deep-set eyes under level hard brows, long grey-streaked hair in a high topknot with blue cloth tails. No sword in frame. Behind him the hall dissolves into warm lamp smoke: dim red pillars, gold autumn light slanting through lattice doors, the young king only a blurred crimson shape at the frame edge. A low autumn sun through the lattice rakes across his face from the side, with Silla blue (#2A5FB8) in the shadows and the silk.

hwanin--dangun-old-joseon.scene: INTRODUCING HWANIN, the Lord of Heaven — he has been watching this peninsula since before it had names. High above everything, before there are any kingdoms: a sea of sunlit cloud at morning, and far below, through a break in it, a great forested mountain and a few threads of smoke from the first villages along the rivers. Low three-quarter angle across the cloud-tops: the old god sits on the edge of the cloud as if on a porch step, leaning forward with one forearm across his knee, and with his other hand draws the clouds apart like a curtain to look down; a fond, sly, faintly amused grandfather's look, eyes crinkled, one corner of the mouth lifting, as if the world has just given him an idea. His face redrawn from the photo-like sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness: a lined, weathered old face, swept-back grey-black hair, a long white goatee and moustache. Plain white ramie robe, loose and creased, wide sleeves lifting in the high wind. Behind him a vast bright morning sky, towering sunlit cumulus, blue distance. The low morning sun at the side rakes warm gold across his face and the white cloth, with ivory (#F4F1E8) in the highlights; no halo, no glow aura.

hwanung--dangun-old-joseon.scene: INTRODUCING HWANUNG, a son of heaven who kept looking down until his father let him go. The summit of Mount Taebaek at the moment he lands under the sacred birch: a huge white-barked birch on bare rock, storm cloud still pouring down around the peak with him, wind tearing at the leaves, a curtain of rain sweeping across the valley below, his followers only hinted at as shapes inside the cloud. Low worm's-eye angle from the rock: he has just touched down, one knee bent on the stone, one hand flat on the birch's white trunk, the other fist holding three small square bronze seals on a cord against his chest, carved faces turned inward, and he lifts his face to the new world with bright, eager, almost disbelieving joy. His face redrawn from the painted sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness: long wavy dark hair blown wild, a full dark beard, warm dark eyes. White robes and a white fur stole, the silk still billowing from the descent. A shaft of sun breaking through the storm rakes across his face from the side in warm gold (#d4b86a); no halo, no glow aura.

ungnyeo--dangun-old-joseon.scene: INTRODUCING UNGNYEO, who was a bear twenty-one days ago — the tiger left first; a husband should be easy. The third evening under the sacred birch on Mount Taebaek, on the path he has to take to reach his hall. Low three-quarter angle from the path: she leans one shoulder against the white birch trunk, arms folded, blocking the way, and tips her chin up at the son of heaven coming up the path (only a blurred white sleeve at the frame edge), with a sly, warm, knowing grin, red lips, one eyebrow raised: "You're going to walk past again." Her face redrawn from the painted sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness: a young woman, black hair in a low knot with loose strands, held by a long bronze hairpin topped with a small carved roaring bear head. White hanbok, a thick brown bear-fur stole around her shoulders, a rust-red sash ribbon. Behind her the birch leaves glow gold, the slope falls away into blue haze, snow on the far peak, drifting pollen as bokeh. The setting sun through the leaves rakes warm gold across her face from the side, with soft tan (#c9b18f) in the fur and the silk.

dangun--dangun-old-joseon.scene: INTRODUCING DANGUN — half heaven, half bear, and all the paperwork of a first king. Asadal, where the mountain meets the plain, on the morning he founds the first city. Low three-quarter angle from the slope: he stands on a rock outcrop above the plain and weighs one heavy square bronze seal in his open palm, carved face turned down, looking out over the new city being laid out below — rammed-earth walls, timber palisades, thatched long halls, cooking smoke — with a wry, patient half-smile, the look of a man who has just counted how much there is to do. His face redrawn from the painted sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness: long black hair loose to the shoulders, a full black beard, strong brows. White robes, a white bear pelt over one shoulder with its head hanging at his chest, a rust-red scarf, leather belts and wrapped forearms. Behind him the mountain rises into morning mist and the plain runs out to a silver river under a wide bright sky. The morning sun from the side rakes warm across his face and the white fur, with warm umber (#b8956a) in the shadows.

daejoyoung--balhae.scene: INTRODUCING DAE JOYOUNG — a boy with frozen feet, and a piece of a crown in the pack. The mountains of Manchuria the winter after Pyongyang falls: snow to the knee, wind off the ridges, a blizzard thinning over dark pines. Low angle from the snow: the boy, about ten, wades forward in his father's deep tracks, leaning hard on his walking staff, and calls out to his father ahead (only a huge fur-wrapped back and a leather pack, blurred at the frame edge), face crumpling: "Father… my feet… I can't feel my feet." A round child's face, dark eyes under heavy brows, cheeks and nose raw red with cold, a frost smudge on one cheek, eyes watering, lips chapped — complaining, but still walking. Red headband with a black sun-disc, brown fur collar, pale blue padded coat, red sash. A child with NO crown on his head: the only gold is hidden inside his father's pack, out of sight. Behind him the snowstorm swirls blue-grey over a pine ridge, a faint smudge of far smoke on the horizon. A pale low sun breaking through the snow cloud rakes across his face from the side, cold gold, with brick red (#c45a4a) in the headband and his cheeks.
